note-1.text:
AUDIENCE AND SCOPE
For partners, owners and account leadership. It shows account-level results only. Message-level detail (top emails, campaigns, source codes) stays in each client's Fundraising Report, one click away in the live build.

note-2.text:
WHO CAN SEE IT
This page shows every client side by side, so it must never be shared with a client. In the live build, limit access to agency leadership. If account directors get a version, filter it to their own accounts.

note-3.text:
METRIC LINEAGE
Every figure is a sum, or a revenue-weighted average, of the same metric in each client's report, for the same dates and channel rules. Raised and vs last year: All Donations. Projection: Scorecard. New donors: Acquisition. Run rate: recurring donors. Raised per $1: Scorecard (texts and ads). Traced share and issues: Data Quality.

note-4.text:
LIKE FOR LIKE
The headline total includes every account. Growth rates, projections against last year and new-donor change leave out accounts with no full prior year; those show 'New this cycle' instead of a misleading +300%. The lede gives both figures, and the caption shows how much one fast-growing campaign moves the total.

note-5.text:
WHERE EACH ACCOUNT STANDS
Status is a shape, a word and a color: ● on track, ■ watch, ▲ at risk. The two threshold lines are dashed and labelled. An account off the scale is pinned to the edge with its real figure. Keyboard: tab to the chart; arrows step through accounts in revenue order; Escape closes. The data table lists every point.

note-6.text:
ACCOUNTS TABLE (try it in Play)
'Show' is a group of toggle buttons (aria-pressed) with counts. 'Showing N of 12 accounts' is visible text and is announced. Sortable headings are buttons with aria-sort; select again to reverse. Accounts with no prior year always sort last. The portfolio row stays fixed whatever the filter.

note-7.text:
STATUS RULE
At risk: projected more than 15% behind last year. Watch: 5–15% behind, or any high-severity data-quality issue, because bad data can hide a real problem. Thresholds should be agency settings that partners can change, shown in the definitions.

note-8.text:
NEEDS ATTENTION
At-risk accounts first, then watch, then new. 'What changed' is generated from each account's report. 'Next step' and 'Review by' are entered and owned by the account director, so this page doubles as the leadership meeting agenda.

note-9.text:
MISSING DATA
A gap never shows as zero. The coverage table names the accounts behind each gap, and an account that fails to load is listed and left out of the totals, with a count beside the headline figures.
